[strategy/guidance/security/Endpoint/GUID-SEC-ENDPOINT-CAP-MAP-0.4.02.md#l1-capability-endpoint-security]

## L1 Capability: Endpoint Security

Endpoint Security is the enterprise security capability that governs the protection, detection, management, and governance of all endpoint devices — workstations, laptops, mobile devices, virtual desktops, and servers — across their full lifecycle. As a critical pillar of the Zero Trust architecture, Endpoint Security provides the device posture signals, configuration assurance, behavioral detection, and privilege controls that are prerequisite inputs to Zero Trust access decisions. It interfaces directly with the Identity Security domain (providing device identity and posture context for access decisions), the Security Operations domain (delivering endpoint telemetry and detection output for threat correlation), and the Network Security domain (providing device health signals that inform network-layer policy enforcement).

[strategy/guidance/security/Endpoint/GUID-SEC-ENDPOINT-CAP-MAP-0.4.02.md#l2-capability-areas]

## L2 Capability Areas

| L2 Capability | Description | Maturity Indicator |
|---|---|---|
| **Endpoint Asset Inventory and Discovery** | Continuous discovery, registration, and lifecycle tracking of all managed endpoint devices; authoritative source of record for device identity, ownership, classification, and managed status across all device populations | Initial |
| **Endpoint Configuration Governance** | Definition, enforcement, and continuous verification of hardening baselines for all managed device populations; detection of configuration drift and governance of the exception and remediation lifecycle | Initial |
| **Endpoint Protection Platform** | Prevention-oriented controls including anti-malware, application control, script blocking, and execution prevention that reduce the probability of successful malware execution and initial access through endpoint attack vectors | Developing |
| **Endpoint Detection and Response** | Behavioral detection, continuous monitoring, threat hunting, investigation, and coordinated response capabilities that identify endpoint-based threats that bypass prevention controls and provide the investigation data needed for effective incident response | Developing |
| **Mobile and Remote Endpoint Management** | Policy enforcement, configuration management, and security monitoring for mobile devices (iOS, Android), remote endpoints, and managed BYOD devices operating outside enterprise perimeter controls | Initial |
| **Endpoint Vulnerability Management** | Systematic discovery, contextualized prioritization, and tracked remediation of vulnerabilities across all managed endpoint operating systems, application software, and firmware; integration with asset inventory to ensure complete coverage | Initial |
| **Device Trust and Posture Assessment** | Collection, evaluation, and continuous communication of device health signals — configuration compliance, patch state, threat detection status, and identity binding — to the Zero Trust Policy Decision Point for incorporation into access decisions | Initial |
| **Endpoint Privilege Management** | Governance of local administrative and elevated privileges on endpoints; enforcement of least-privilege and just-enough-access principles; time-bounded privilege elevation workflows that eliminate standing administrative access on managed workstations and laptops | Initial |
| **Endpoint Data Protection** | Protection of data at rest on endpoint devices through encryption; prevention of unauthorized data exfiltration through removable media, local printing, and endpoint-accessible cloud sync channels; integration with enterprise data classification | Developing |
| **Endpoint Telemetry and Analytics** | Centralized collection, normalization, and forwarding of endpoint security events, behavioral signals, and audit logs; establishment of behavioral baselines for anomaly detection; integration with the enterprise security information and event platform for threat correlation | Developing |

## Scope and Boundaries

**In Scope**: Governance and security of all managed endpoint device populations across their full lifecycle; configuration, detection, protection, privilege management, data protection, and telemetry capabilities for all managed endpoints; device posture data flows to Zero Trust access control infrastructure

**Out of Scope**:
- Identity lifecycle management, authentication, and authorization decisions (see [Identity Security — GUID-SEC-IAM-REF-2.2.01](../Identity/GUID-SEC-IAM-REF-2.2.01.md))
- Network segmentation, firewall policy, and network-layer access control (see Network Security domain)
- Data classification, enterprise DLP at the data platform layer, and data governance (see Information Security domain)
- Security Operations detection, triage, and response workflows beyond endpoint telemetry forwarding (see Security Operations domain)
- OT/ICS/SCADA device security specific to operational technology environments
- Physical access control and hardware supply chain assurance
- Security standards, configuration baselines, and control mandates (belong in `standards/security/`)
- Vendor product selection and Solution Building Blocks (Phase E–F)

[strategy/guidance/security/Endpoint/GUID-SEC-ENDPOINT-CAP-MAP-0.4.02.md#cross-domain-capability-interfaces]

## Cross-Domain Capability Interfaces

| Adjacent Domain | Interface Description | Direction |
|---|---|---|
| **Identity Security** ([GUID-SEC-IAM-REF-2.2.01](../Identity/GUID-SEC-IAM-REF-2.2.01.md)) | Device posture assessment signals (compliance state, patch level, EDR status) are passed to the Identity/Zero Trust access decision layer as device-conditional access inputs; device certificates issued by endpoint management are consumed by identity federation | Endpoint → Identity |
| **Security Operations** | Endpoint telemetry, EDR alerts, and behavioral detection output are forwarded to the SIEM/SOAR platform for correlation, triage, and response workflow initiation | Endpoint → SecOps |
| **Network Security** | Device health and managed-status signals inform network access control and segmentation policies; posture non-compliance may trigger network quarantine | Endpoint → Network |
| **Information Security** | Endpoint data protection capabilities (encryption, DLP, media control) enforce data classification policies originating from the Information Security domain | Information → Endpoint |
| **Vulnerability Management** | Endpoint vulnerability discovery data feeds the enterprise vulnerability management program; remediation prioritization consumes threat intelligence from SecOps | Bidirectional |
